Hi Mina,

Thanks for kicking off the onboarding. Our legal and security teams need two quick confirmations before we proceed to procurement: 

1) A written, per-tenant "no-training" commitment for customer-supplied prompts/responses (we need language we can attach to our DPA).
2) Proof that KMS keys for MedNova can be provisioned and kept in US regions only (we need the KMS residency and key lifecycle controls spelled out).

Also: can you provide an evidence pack showing where prompt/response logs are stored, retention defaults, and any operational steps to produce a tamper-evident export if required by auditors?

Attached is our standard compliance questionnaire (mednova-compliance-q1.pdf). Would prefer to get this back by Friday so procurement can finalize the PO.

Appreciate the help — looping in Compliance.

Best,
Julia He
Head of Security Programs
MedNova Health

Subject: Re: No-training verification & KMS residency — MedNova onboarding

Hi Julia — thanks for the clear ask and the questionnaire. Short answers up front: 

- No-training commitment: we provide an opt-out / "no model improvement" guarantee per tenant. We will not use customer prompt/response content to update or fine-tune any shared or internal model weights unless explicitly authorized in writing. We can provide a short clause suitable for a DPA and an operational certificate (signed by our security lead) that attests to the configuration in your tenant.

- KMS residency: we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) and Redwood-managed keys with region scoping. For MedNova we can restrict key creation and storage to US regions only (we use separate regional key rings and HSM-backed providers).

What I'll do next:
1) Draft a DPA clause and attach our operational attestation.
2) Pull together an evidence pack (kms-config and an ops checklist) showing where logs are retained, the export path, and retention defaults.
3) Loop in David and Dev for the technical specifics the questionnaire asks for.

Can you confirm whether the keys should be customer-managed in your own KMS (we'll accept a key reference) or if you prefer Redwood-managed keys restricted to US? That will change the operational steps we include.

I'll target an initial evidence bundle by EOD Thursday.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Julia He <julia.he@mednova.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: No-training verification & KMS residency — MedNova onboarding

Julia / Mina — technical detail dump to include in the evidence pack (summary first, then specifics):

Summary: Redwood supports tenant-level isolation and a no-training mode. When that mode is enabled for a tenant: 
- Inference requests are processed by dedicated runtime pools or logically isolated execution contexts; no telemetry from those requests is included in model updates.
- Request logs (request metadata, timestamps) are retained per the tenant's retention policy; full prompt/response bodies can be configured to be ephemeral and excluded from longer-term telemetry.

KMS / keys: 
- Option A (Customer-managed): MedNova provides a customer key (ARN) in their KMS. Redwood never stores the plaintext key; we call the KMS for sign/decrypt operations. Keys live in the customer-owned US region (we support us-east-1, us-west-2).
- Option B (Redwood-managed, US-only): Redwood provisions keys on HSM-backed key rings restricted to US region(s). We can provide an exportable key reference and the key rotation policy.

Operational artifacts we will attach:
- kms-config-20261021.pdf: diagram showing key flow, regional restrictions, and HSM provider.
- evidence-checklist-ntv.xlsx: step-by-step checklist (how to verify tenant is in no-training mode, sample API call to confirm, retention settings to assert ephemeral storage).

Logs and exports: 
- Prompt/response bodies: we can mark as ephemeral (default TTL 72 hours) and provide an authenticated export endpoint for audit requests. Exports include an audit log with signature and timeline.
- Tamper-evidence: exports include an event hash chain and signature; we can produce a signed export bundle on request.

Proofs we can provide for auditors: signed attestation (.pdf), sample export bundle, and a copy of the tenant's runtime configuration (no-training flag status).

Open items for MedNova to confirm: 
1) Preferred KMS model (customer-owned vs Redwood-managed US-only).
2) Desired retention for prompt/response bodies if different from default.
3) Whether the procurement team needs a one-sentence DPA addendum or a redline to their standard DPA.

If helpful, we can also schedule a 30-minute tech walkthrough this week to run through the evidence artifacts and a live export.

Regards,
David Kim
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Mina and David — that level of detail is perfect. A couple quick follow-ups: 

- We'll go with Option A (customer-managed KMS) and will provide an ARN next week. Please include the sample API call we can run to confirm the key mapping once we hand the ARN over.
- Retention: set prompt/response bodies to ephemeral 72 hours for now; procurement may ask for a shorter TTL later but this is acceptable to start.
- For the DPA: procurement wants a two-sentence addendum that explicitly states "MedNova content will not be used to improve or train Redwood models absent explicit written consent." If you can send that clause as plain text we can attach it and avoid a redline.

We also want the signed operational attestation for our file. If you can add the attestation to the evidence bundle (signed PDF) we'll route it to procurement and legal.

I'll upload the initial questionnaire responses once I cross-check your checklist. Also linking our procurement DocuSign template for the PO flow: https://app.docusign.com/templates/abc123-def456

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to set the tech walkthrough for Thursday if that works for you.

Best,
Julia
Head of Security Programs, MedNova Health
